pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should your composed rhythm be your own idea? (1 mark)
   A. To be different from the teacher only
   B. To use more paper
   C. To finish faster
   D. Original work shows honesty

2. Variation in a melody means using (1 mark)
   A. only rests
   B. different syllables and note lengths
   C. only one syllable
   D. no rhythm

3. The Kenya National Anthem is called (1 mark)
   A. Jambo Bwana
   B. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   C. Malaika
   D. Twinkle Twinkle Little Star

4. In an elongated start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the heel of the front foot
   B. the start line
   C. the toes of the front foot
   D. the front knee

5. The French rhythm name for a pair of quavers is (1 mark)
   A. ta-te
   B. tee-taa
   C. rest
   D. taa

6. What should you do after passing the ball? (1 mark)
   A. Sit down
   B. Move into space to receive it again
   C. Walk off the court
   D. Close your eyes

7. A swimming cap is useful for (1 mark)
   A. making you float
   B. drying
   C. holding a whistle
   D. keeping long hair out of the way

8. Claves are (1 mark)
   A. drums with strings
   B. a kind of flute
   C. two wooden sticks hit together
   D. a horn

9. Which muscles does the crab balance mainly strengthen? (1 mark)
   A. Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   B. Only the fingers
   C. Only the eyes
   D. Only the ears

10. Isukuti is a lively drum dance of the (1 mark)
   A. Maasai
   B. Luhya
   C. Somali
   D. Turkana

11. Why should you write the date on each work in your portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. To spoil it
   B. For fun only
   C. To hide it
   D. To show when it was made

12. The game restarts after each goal with (1 mark)
   A. a jump ball
   B. a centre pass
   C. a throw-in from the side
   D. a penalty kick

13. On the staff, the note G sits on (1 mark)
   A. line 3
   B. a space above the staff
   C. line 2
   D. the top line

14. Which move is a step? (1 mark)
   A. m to d in one jump over r
   B. d to m
   C. d to r
   D. d to d

15. Which is part of a good warm-up? (1 mark)
   A. Gentle jogging and stretching
   B. Sitting still
   C. Eating a large meal
   D. Sleeping

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. How do you care for a paint brush? (3 marks)

17. Compose a four-beat rhythmic pattern using a crotchet, a pair of quavers and a rest, and write it in rhythm names. (4 marks)

18. Explain where the sun should be when you photograph a person and why. (3 marks)

19. Describe how to make a ball using the macramé technique and overhand knots. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Original work shows honesty
   Creating your own pattern shows integrity.

2. B — different syllables and note lengths
   Variation makes a tune interesting.

3. B — Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   The Kiswahili title is Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu.

4. A — the heel of the front foot
   The elongated start puts the knee further back, by the heel of the front foot.

5. A — ta-te
   Ta-te is two short sounds in one beat.

6. B — Move into space to receive it again
   Moving into open space keeps the game flowing.

7. D — keeping long hair out of the way
   Caps keep hair tidy.

8. C — two wooden sticks hit together
   Claves are two hardwood sticks that are struck together.

9. A — Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   Holding the body up uses many muscle groups.

10. B — Luhya
   Isukuti is played by the Luhya people, especially the Isukha and Idakho.

11. D — To show when it was made
   Dates show how your skills grow.

12. B — a centre pass
   The game restarts with a centre pass, and the teams take turns.

13. C — line 2
   G is on the second line from the bottom with the treble clef.

14. C — d to r
   Doh to ray is to the next note.

15. A — Gentle jogging and stretching
   Jogging and stretching prepare the body.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rinse when changing colour, wash with soap after use, shape the tip and store it flat or with hairs up. Never leave it standing on its hairs in water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example taa ta-te (rest) taa. Any four-beat pattern with all three parts and ending on a crotchet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four beats, 1 mark for using all three, 1 mark for correct names, 1 mark for ending on a long note.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind the photographer, so light falls on the front of the person. If the sun is behind the subject, the face is in shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 2 marks for the reason.

19. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a firm core from paper or cloth. Cut equal cords. Tie them together with an overhand knot at the middle. Put the core on top. Tie overhand knots between pairs of neighbouring cords to make a net around the core. Gather the cords at the bottom and tie a strong knot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear stages.
